method: headless py3.11 render of :8031/live-copy (domcontentloaded + readyState poll, 16 rows), plus TestClient/ConfigManager probes on the same source tree; two-process restart test on an isolated HL_LIVE_AUDIT_DIR

rows.why: OD-13 unruled and the tombstone clause has no route: the exact missing component is LiveCopyCore close management for archived sleeves. Archive/restore config semantics do pass (remove-wallet archive:true writes archived_wallets with archived_at, mode OFF, enabled False; set-mode restores into wallets), but ConfigManager.wallets() drops archived wallets entirely, so an archived wallet cannot follow closes; the only related handling is archived_manual_residuals accounting (action NO_ACTION_ARCHIVED_LEDGER_RESIDUAL_ACCOUNTED).

Row-bound mutation on one wallet+fill: before enable, IntentBuilder._decision(ENTRY) = BLOCKED_OFF 'wallet disabled'; after POST /api/live-config/set-mode LIVE (config mode LIVE, enabled true) the same call returns ENTRY_ALLOWED. ConfigManager maps LIVE->ON. No catch-up key is written on enable (catchup/backfill keys absent), matching 'next genuine post-change event only'.

Disable blocks new entries but does not keep owned exposure managed: with mode OFF / enabled false, IntentBuilder._decision(EXIT) returns BLOCKED_OFF 'wallet disabled', so a leader close on an already-owned sleeve is refused rather than followed. The row requires existing owned exposure to remain safely managed after disable.

Row-bound on the same wallet+fill: CLO -> ENTRY=BLOCKED_CLO_ENTRY and ADD=BLOCKED_CLO_ENTRY, while EXIT=EXIT_ALLOWED; switching the same wallet to LIVE gives ENTRY_ALLOWED. Config round-trips mode CLO to a fresh process and CLO stays in the active set (wallet_mode CLO, enabled true).

copy_mode does persist and reach the engine (ConfigManager.copy_mode reads proportional/fixed), but the row's UI obligation is unmet: the served Live Copy panel contains no HOLD / fail-closed / OD-02 statement anywhere, and wallets persisted as copy_mode=fixed render as ordinary LIVE rows with no warning (DOM row 0x010461c1...1c703a: mode=LIVE, copy_mode=fixed, plain row, only generic prop|fixed selector).

Row-bound: norm_base=321 written via /api/live-config/set-wallet is read back as 321.0 by a fresh ConfigManager while fixed_notional stays 12.5, so the value is per-key and persists; norm_base=-5 is clamped to 1.0 (not silently dropped) and a non-numeric norm_base falls back without corrupting the stored value.

Persistence passes (fixed_notional 12.5 written by the UI is read back by a fresh ConfigManager), but 'used only by ruled fixed semantics' cannot be asserted while OD-02 is unruled. The exact unruled component is IntentBuilder._copy_notional's fixed branch (fixed_notional * merged_fill_count), which is live for every wallet currently stored as copy_mode=fixed.

leader_equity_base does not persist through any UI write path: POST /api/wallet-config with leader_equity_base=50000 returns 200 but ui_state.wallet_config stores only copy_mode/norm_base/fixed_notional (value dropped), and /api/live-config/set-wallet leaves the config value null. The engine additionally lists it in ENGINE_IGNORED_WALLET_KEYS, so '>= 1 persists and is a sizing input' is not met on the persist half.

Row-bound DOM read of the served panel (16 rows) shows per-wallet, not boilerplate, values in every required field: mode label, connection/health cell, exposure + open position count, and last-fill target. Distinctness that a single shared sweep could not produce: 0x936cf4fb exposure $1,928.19 / 15 pos / DD -$27.47 vs 0xc179e039 $161.23 / 4 pos / DD -$25 vs 0x1b232b41 $0 / 0 pos / 'none yet'; OFF rows show 'not followed' while LIVE rows show 'Websocket OK | HOT10 shared socket active'.

Real two-process restart: process A wrote mode=CLO, enabled=true, copy_mode=proportional, norm_base=321, fixed_notional=12.5 through the HTTP write path; a separate process B constructing ConfigManager over the same live_config.json returned exactly CLO/true/proportional/321.0/12.5. No send_attempts.csv was created in the isolated audit dir, so restart created no orders.

Row-bound reject/clamp matrix executed against the live routes: invalid address -> 400 BAD_WALLET; mode NONSENSE -> 400 BAD_MODE; copy_mode nonsense -> 400 BAD_COPY_MODE; norm_base -5 -> clamped to 1.0 (from 250.0); fixed_notional 'abc' -> stored value unchanged (10). Each rejected call left the rest of the persisted wallet block untouched, and the panel's jpost path surfaces err.message to the operator.

Only the legacy writer enforces the rule: /api/set-wallet-mode on the user wallet returns mode OFF and /api/admin/purge-wallet returns 400 CANNOT_PURGE_USER_WALLET. The Live Copy writer does not: POST /api/live-config/add-wallet with the user wallet and mode LIVE returns 200, persists {mode LIVE, enabled true}, and a fresh ConfigManager reports the user wallet in active_wallets() with wallet_mode ON. The account wallet is therefore enableable through the UI route.

The two writers still contradict each other with no reconciliation: /api/set-wallet-mode ON wrote wallet_gate.json {mode ON}, then /api/live-config/set-mode OFF wrote live_config.json {mode OFF} for the same wallet, and both files stayed contradictory (gate ON, config OFF). The engine reads live_config (OFF) while the gate surface says ON, so contradictory authority is reachable and OD-05 remains unresolved.

OD-13 unruled and no exposure guard exists to test: purge_wallet_everywhere refuses only the user wallet (CANNOT_PURGE_USER_WALLET) and otherwise deletes the wallet from config/audit/derived files unconditionally; purging a non-user wallet returned 200 with no exposure check. The required 'refused or safe when the wallet owns exposure' branch is absent, so the row cannot be certified either way.

Row-bound side-effect test: POST /api/wallet-include for a wallet writes only ui_state.wallet_include ({wallet: true}); that wallet's live_config block keeps its own mode unchanged (OFF before and after), and the engine source contains zero wallet_include references, so the toggle cannot reach sizing or order paths. It only feeds panel aggregation (wallet_included / portfolio_wallets).
